pages.text: "I'll watch from here!" Mei the timid baby goat sat on a wide rock by the stream. Ppino the rabbit, always first at everything, already splashed in the pool. Mei held both scarf ends tightly.
"I want to play somewhere cool too..." Mei stretched a toe toward the water, then pulled it back. They couldn't see how deep it was.
The sun blazed. The rock grew hotter and hotter. Mei shifted their feet from one spot to another. "Ouch, hot! My soles are warm!"
Ppino laughed and splashed in the water. Mei was alone on the rock. No shade, and their feet stayed hot.
Mei climbed down to the pool edge. But as soon as a toe touched water, their body flinched. "I still can't."
Grandma Bear sat beside Mei with her feet in the pool. Water rippled at her ankles. "Mei, can you see how high the water comes?"
Grandma pointed to two places on the rock. "Here are ankles, here are knees. No farther than that." Mei repeated, "Ankles first, then knees!"
Mei stepped down, one foot, then two. Water rippled at their ankles. "Oh! Cool!" Their hot soles cooled at once. Grandma's hand stayed beside them.
Splashing, Mei counted loudly. "One, to my ankles! Two, then my knees! Three, no farther!" Water rippled at Mei's knees.
Mei and Ppino splashed in the pool. Grandma patted Mei's wet back. Go in little by little, and scary water feels cool. Holding Ppino's hand, Mei said, "Ankles first, then knees!"
